questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements : i. A private member's bill is a bill presented by a Member of Parliament who is not elected but only nominated by the President of India. 2. Recently, a private member's bill has been passed in the Parliament of India for the first time in its history. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: A private member's bill is introduced by an MP who is NOT a minister (elected members, not "nominated by President" — statement 1 is wrong on both counts). Several private member's bills have been passed historically (e.g., in 1956, 1970), so "first time" in statement 2 is false.

questions.subject: Ancient History
questions.question: With reference to the difference between the culture of Rigvedic Aryans and Indus Valley people, which of the following statements is/are correct ? 1. Rigvedic Aryans used the coat of mail and helmet in warfare whereas the people of Indus Valley Civilization did not leave any evidence of using them. 2. Rigvedic Aryans knew gold, silver and copper whereas Indus Valley people knew only copper and iron. 3. Rigvedic Aryans had domesticated the horse whereas there is no evidence of Indus Valley people having been aware of this animal. Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.explanation: Rigvedic Aryans used coat of mail/helmet (kavacha, sipra) in warfare with no IVC evidence of these; they had domesticated horses (frequent Rigvedic references) while IVC has no confirmed horse evidence. However, IVC knew copper, but Rigvedic Aryans knew gold, silver AND copper — IVC also had access to iron is disputed/wrong (IVC was a Bronze Age civilization, no iron); hence statement 2 is incorrect.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: 'Recognition of Prior Learning Scheme' is sometimes mentioned in the news with reference to
options: Certifying the skills acquired by construction workers through traditional channels.
Enrolling the persons in Universities for distance learning programmes.
Reserving some skilled jobs to rural and urban poor in some public sector undertakings.
Certifying the skills acquired by trainees under the National Skill Development Programme.
questions.explanation: The Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) scheme under the Skill India Mission certifies and standardizes skills acquired informally/traditionally (like construction workers), not through formal training programs.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: From the ecological point of view, which one of the following assumes importance in being a good link between the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve in Tamil Nadu is a crucial wildlife corridor linking the Eastern Ghats and Western Ghats, enabling elephant and tiger movement between the two ranges.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: One of the implications of equality in society is the absence of
questions.explanation: Equality means the absence of special privileges for any section of society along with adequate opportunities for all — it does not mean absence of restraints, competition, or ideology.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: Consider the following statements in respect of Trade Related Analysis of Fauna and Flora in Commerce (TRAFFIC) : 1. TRAFFIC is a bureau under United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). 2. The mission of TRAFFIC is to ensure that trade in wild plants and animals is not a threat to the conservation of nature. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: TRAFFIC is a joint programme of WWF and IUCN, NOT a UN body (statement 1 wrong). Its mission is indeed to ensure wildlife trade doesn't threaten conservation (statement 2 correct).

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Which principle among the following was added to the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution?
options: Equal pay for equal work for both men and women
Participation of workers in the management of industries
Right to work, education and public assistance
Securing living wage and human conditions of work to workers
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Article 43A, directing the State to secure worker participation in management of industries, among other new DPSPs.

questions.subject: Ancient History
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Rights are claims of the State against the citizens.
Rights are privileges which are incorporated in the Constitution of a State.
Rights are claims of the citizens against the State.
Rights are privileges of a few citizens against the many.
questions.explanation: Rights are entitlements citizens hold against the State, which is obligated to protect them — not privileges or claims of the State against citizens.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Of the following, which gives 'Global Gender Gap Index' ranking to the countries of the world?
questions.explanation: The WEF publishes the annual Global Gender Gap Report ranking countries on gender parity across economic, political, education, and health criteria.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Smart India Hackathon 2017? 1. It is a centrally sponsored scheme for developing every city of our country into Smart Cities in a decade. 2. It is an initiative to identify new digital technology innovations for solving the many problems faced by our country. 3. It is a programme aimed at making all the financial transactions in our country completely digital in a decade. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Smart India Hackathon is a nationwide initiative to solve pressing problems through digital innovation and technology — it is not a Smart Cities scheme (1 wrong) nor purely about digital payments (3 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)? 1. It decides the RBI's benchmark interest rates. 2. It is a 12-member body including the Governor of RBI and is reconstituted every year. 3. It functions under the chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: The MPC (6 members, not 12) decides the repo rate/policy rates, and is chaired by the RBI Governor, not the Finance Minister — so statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: With reference to Manipuri Sankirtana, consider the following statements: 1. It is a song and dance performance. 2. Cymbals are the only musical instruments used in the performance. 3. It is performed to narrate the life and deeds of Lord Krishna. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Manipuri Sankirtana is a devotional song-dance performance narrating Krishna's life; it uses multiple instruments including mridanga/pung and cymbals, not cymbals alone (statement 2 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Who among the following was/were associated with the introduction of Ryotwari Settlement in India during the British rule ? 1. Lord Cornwallis 2. Alexander Read 3. Thomas Munro Select the correct answer using.the code given below :
questions.explanation: Alexander Read pioneered the Ryotwari system in Baramahal, later systematized by Thomas Munro in Madras Presidency. Lord Cornwallis is associated with the Permanent (Zamindari) Settlement, not Ryotwari.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: In the context of solving pollution problems, what is/are the advantage/advantages of bioremediation technique? 1. It is a technique for cleaning up pollution by enhancing the same biodegradation process that occurs in nature. 2. Any contaminant with heavy metals such as cadmium and lead can be readily and completely treated by bioremediation using microorganisms. 3. Genetic engineering can be used to create microorganisms specifically designed for bioremediation. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Bioremediation enhances natural biodegradation (1 correct) and genetic engineering can create designer microbes for it (3 correct). However, heavy metals like cadmium/lead cannot be biodegraded — they can only be immobilized/bioaccumulated, not "completely treated" (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The Trade Disputes Act of 1929 provided for
options: the participation of workers in the management of industries.
arbitrary powers to the management to quell industrial disputes.
an intervention by the British Court in the event of a trade dispute.
a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes.
questions.explanation: The Trade Disputes Act, 1929 established a mechanism of Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation, and restricted strikes in public utility services.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Local self-government can be best explained as an exercise in
questions.explanation: Local self-government (Panchayati Raj/Municipalities) represents devolution of power to grassroots elected bodies — the essence of democratic decentralisation.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: With reference to the Constitution of India, the Directive Principles of State Policy constitute limitations upon 1. legislative function. 2. executive function. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: DPSPs (Part IV) are not legally enforceable limitations on legislative or executive functions — they are non-justiciable guiding principles, not restrictions.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: The term 'Digital Single Market Strategy' seen in the news refers to
questions.explanation: The Digital Single Market Strategy is a European Union initiative aimed at breaking down digital barriers to create a unified digital market across EU member states.

questions.subject: Modern History
questions.question: At one of the places in India, if you stand on the seashore and watch the sea, you will find that the sea water recedes from the shore line a few kilometres and comes back to the shore, twice a day, and you can actually walk on the sea floor when the water recedes. This unique phenomenon is seen at
questions.explanation: At Chandipur beach in Odisha, the sea recedes several kilometres during low tide and returns, allowing people to walk on the exposed sea floor — a unique tidal phenomenon.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: With reference to the ‘Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (PBPT Act)’, consider the following statements : 1. A property transaction is not treated as a benami transaction if the owner of the property is not aware of the transaction. 2. Properties held benami are liable for confiscation by the Government. 3. The Act provides for three authorities for investigations but does not provide for any appellate mechanism. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Benami properties are liable for confiscation under the PBPT Act (2 correct). A transaction can still be "benami" even if the real owner isn't directly involved in daily dealings (1 wrong), and the Act does provide for an Appellate Tribunal (3 wrong).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: Due to some reasons, if there is a huge fall in the population of species of butterflies, what could be its likely consequence/consequences? 1. Pollination of some plants could be adversely affected. 2. There could be a drastic increase in the fungal infections of some cultivated plants. 3. It could lead to a fall in the population of some species of wasps, spiders and birds. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Butterflies are key pollinators, so their decline affects pollination (1 correct) and food chains involving predators like birds/spiders/wasps that depend on butterfly larvae/adults (3 correct). Fungal infection increase (2) isn't a recognized ecological consequence of butterfly decline.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: It is possible to produce algae-based biofuels, but what is/are the likely limitation(s) of developing countries in promoting this industry? 1. Production of algae-based biofuels is possible in seas only and not on continents. 2. Setting up and engineering the algae-based biofuel production requires high level of expertise/technology until the construction is completed. 3. Economically viable production necessitates the setting up of large-scale facilities which may raise ecological and social concerns. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Algae biofuel production requires significant technical expertise (2) and large-scale facilities raise ecological/social concerns (3). However, algae can be cultivated on land too (in ponds/photobioreactors), not seas only (1 wrong).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Which of the following are the objectives of ‘National Nutrition Mission’? 1. To create awareness relating to malnutrition among pregnant women and lactating mothers. 2. To reduce the incidence of anaemia among young children, adolescent girls and women. 3. To promote the consumption of millets, coarse cereals and unpolished rice. 4. To promote the consumption of poultry eggs. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: The National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyaan) targets awareness on malnutrition among pregnant/lactating women (1) and reducing anaemia (2). It doesn't specifically mandate promotion of millets or poultry eggs consumption (3, 4 wrong).

questions.subject: Modern History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Factories Act, 1881 was passed with a view to fix the wages of industrial workers and to allow the workers to form trade unions. 2. N. M. Lokhande was a pioneer in organizing the labour movement in British India. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: N.M. Lokhande indeed pioneered India's labour movement, founding the Bombay Mill Hands Association. The Factories Act, 1881 regulated child labour and factory conditions — it did NOT fix wages or permit trade unions (1 wrong).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: In the context of mitigating the impending global warming due to anthropogenic emissions of carbon dioxide, which of the following can be the potential sites for carbon sequestration? 1. Abandoned and uneconomic coal seams 2. Depleted oil and gas reservoirs 3. Subterranean deep saline formations Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: All three — depleted coal seams, oil/gas reservoirs, and deep saline aquifers — are recognized geological sites for carbon capture and storage (CCS).

questions.subject: Modern History
questions.question: The object of the Butler Committee of 1927 was to
options: Define the jurisdiction of the Central and Provincial Governments.
Define the powers of the Secretary of State for India.
Improve the relationship between the Government of India and the Indian States.
questions.explanation: The Butler Committee (1927), also called the Indian States Committee, examined and sought to clarify relations between the paramount power (British Crown) and the Princely States.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The term ‘Domestic Content Requirement’ is sometimes seen in the news with reference to
options: Developing solar power production in our country
Granting licences to foreign T.V. channels in our country
Exporting our food products to other countries
Permitting foreign educational institutions to set up their campuses in our country
questions.explanation: Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) under India's solar policy (Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission) mandates use of domestically manufactured solar cells/modules to boost indigenous manufacturing.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Nuclear Security Summits are periodically held under the aegis of the United Nations. 2. The International Panel on Fissile Materials is an organ of International Atomic Energy Agency. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Nuclear Security Summits were standalone summits (2010-2016) held outside the UN framework, not under UN aegis (1 wrong). The International Panel on Fissile Materials is an independent research group, not part of IAEA (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Who among the following can join the National Pension System (NPS)?
options: Persons of age from 21 to 55 only
All State Government employees joining the services after the date of notification by the respective State Governments
All Central Government employees including those of Armed Forces joining the services on or after 1st April, 2004
questions.explanation: NPS covers all central government employees (from 2004) and state government employees from the date each state notifies adoption — not restricted by residency/age alone, making (c) the accurate description among options.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: With reference to river Teesta, consider the following statements: 1. The source of river Teesta is the same as that of Brahmaputra but it flows through Sikkim. 2. River Rangeet originates in Sikkim and it is a tributary of river Teesta. 3. River Teesta flows into Bay of Bengal on the border of India and Bangladesh. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: River Rangeet originates in Sikkim and is a tributary of Teesta (2 correct). Teesta's source is different from Brahmaputra's (1 wrong), and Teesta joins the Brahmaputra system in Bangladesh, not directly flowing into the Bay of Bengal at the India-Bangladesh border (3 wrong).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. In tropical regions, Zika virus disease is transmitted by the same mosquito that transmits dengue. 2. Sexual transmission of Zika virus disease is possible. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Zika virus is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, the same vector as dengue (1 correct), and sexual transmission of Zika has been documented (2 correct).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Standard Mark of Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is mandatory for automotive tyres and tubes. 2. AGMARK is a quality Certification Mark issued by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: BIS Standard Mark is mandatory for automotive tyres/tubes under quality control orders (1 correct). AGMARK is issued by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection under India's Ministry of Agriculture, not by the FAO (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: What is/are the advantage/advantages of implementing the 'National Agriculture Market' scheme? 1. It is a pan-India electronic trading portal for agricultural commodities. 2. It provides the farmers access to nationwide market, with prices commensurate with the quality of their produce. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market) is indeed a pan-India electronic trading platform (1) that gives farmers wider market access with quality-based pricing (2).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: With reference to the 'National Intellectual Property Rights Policy', consider the following statements: 1. It reiterates India's commitment to the Doha Development Agenda and the TRIPS Agreement. 2. Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion is the nodal agency for regulating intellectual property rights in India. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The National IPR Policy (2016) reaffirms India's commitment to TRIPS and the Doha Development Agenda (1), and designates DIPP (now DPIIT) as the nodal agency for IPR issues (2).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: According to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which of the following animals cannot be hunted by any person except under some provisions provided by law? 1. Gharial 2. Indian wild ass 3. Wild buffalo Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Gharial, Indian wild ass, and wild buffalo are all listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, granting them the highest level of protection.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are true of the Fundamental Duties of an Indian citizen? 1. A legislative process has been provided to enforce these duties. 2. They are correlative to legal duties. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) are not legally enforceable — there's no legislative mechanism to enforce them directly (1 wrong), and they are moral/civic obligations, not correlative legal duties in the strict legal sense (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Modern History
questions.question: Consider the following pairs: 1. Radhakanta Deb — First President of the British Indian Association 2. Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty — Founder of the Madras Mahajana Sabha 3. Surendranath Banerjee — Founder of the Indian Association Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Radhakanta Deb was the first president of the British Indian Association, and Surendranath Banerjee founded the Indian Association. Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association, not the Madras Mahajana Sabha (which was founded by M. Veeraraghavachariar and others).

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Which one of the following objectives is not embodied in the Preamble to the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: The Preamble mentions liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship — but does not explicitly mention "economic liberty" as a value.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: With reference to ‘Quality Council of India (QCI)’, consider the following statements: 1. QCI was set up jointly by the Government of India and the Indian Industry. 2. Chairman of QCI is appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendations of the industry to the Government. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: QCI was set up as a joint initiative of the Government of India and Indian industry (1), and its Chairman is appointed by the Prime Minister based on industry recommendations (2).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: What is the purpose of setting up of Small Finance Banks (SFBs) in India? 1. To supply credit to small business units 2. To supply credit to small and marginal farmers 3. To encourage young entrepreneurs to set up business particularly in rural areas. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Small Finance Banks aim to provide credit to small business units and small/marginal farmers, underserved segments (1, 2). They aren't specifically designed to encourage young rural entrepreneurship as a stated objective (3 not a core aim).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: With reference to ‘Asia Pacific Ministerial Conference on Housing and Urban Development (APMCHUD)’, consider the following statements: 1. The first APMCHUD was held in India in 2006 on the theme ‘Emerging Urban Forms — Policy Responses and Governance Structure’. 2. India hosts all the Annual Ministerial Conferences in partnership with ADB, APEC and ASEAN. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The first APMCHUD was held in India in 2006, but on a different theme than stated (topic details vary from the claim), and India doesn't host all annual conferences — different countries have hosted subsequent editions, making both statements inaccurate as framed.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Democracy’s superior virtue lies in the fact that it calls into activity
options: the intelligence and character of ordinary men and women.
the methods for strengthening executive leadership.
a superior individual with dynamism and vision.
a band of dedicated party workers.
questions.explanation: Democracy's core virtue is that it engages the common citizenry's judgment and participation, rather than relying on an elite few or bureaucratic mechanisms.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a most likely consequence of implementing the ‘Unified Payments Interface (UPI)’?
options: Mobile wallets will not be necessary for online payments.
Digital currency will totally replace the physical currency in about two decades.
Direct transfer of subsidies to poor people will become very effective.
questions.explanation: UPI enables direct bank-to-bank transfers via a single app/identifier, reducing dependence on separate mobile wallets for digital transactions.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The terms 'Event Horizon', 'Singularity', 'String Theory' and 'Standard Model' are sometimes seen in the news in the context of
options: Observation and understanding of the Universe
Study of the solar and the lunar eclipses
Placing satellites in the orbit of the Earth
Origin and evolution of living organisms on the Earth
questions.explanation: Event Horizon, Singularity, String Theory, and Standard Model are all concepts from theoretical physics and cosmology related to understanding the universe's structure and origins.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: With reference to agriculture in India, how can the technique of 'genome sequencing', often seen in the news, be used in the immediate future? 1. Genome sequencing can be used to identify genetic markers for disease resistance and drought tolerance in various crop plants. 2. This technique helps in reducing the time required to develop new varieties of crop plants. 3. It can be used to decipher the host-pathogen relationships in crops. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Genome sequencing helps identify disease/drought-resistance markers (1), speeds up crop variety development (2), and helps understand host-pathogen interactions (3) — all valid near-term agricultural applications.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: The main advantage of the parliamentary form of government is that
options: the executive and legislature work independently.
it provides continuity of policy and is more efficient.
the executive remains responsible to the legislature.
the head of the government cannot be changed without election.
questions.explanation: The defining feature of the parliamentary system is that the executive (Council of Ministers) is collectively responsible and accountable to the legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: In the context of India, which one of the following is the correct relationship between Rights and Duties?
options: Rights are personal and hence independent of society and Duties.
Rights, not Duties, are important for the advancement of the personality of the citizen.
Duties, not Rights, are important for the stability of the State.
questions.explanation: In the Indian constitutional context, rights and duties are seen as two sides of the same coin — every right implies a corresponding duty.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: The mind of the makers of the Constitution of India is reflected in which of the following?
options: The Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.explanation: The Preamble encapsulates the philosophy and vision of the Constitution's framers — its objectives and ideals.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: If you travel by road from Kohima to Kottayam, what is the minimum number of States within India through which you can travel, including the origin and the destination?
questions.explanation: Travelling from Kohima (Nagaland) to Kottayam (Kerala) by road requires passing through a minimum of 7 states given India's geography and highway network.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: The Parliament of India exercises control over the functions of the Council of Ministers through 1. Adjournment motion 2. Question hour 3. Supplementary questions Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Parliament controls the Council of Ministers through adjournment motions, question hour, and supplementary questions — all recognized parliamentary control mechanisms.

questions.subject: Medieval History
questions.question: Which one of the following was a very important seaport in the Kakatiya kingdom?
questions.explanation: Motupalli was a major seaport of the Kakatiya kingdom in coastal Andhra, known for maritime trade, as noted by Marco Polo.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: With reference to 'Global Climate Change Alliance', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. It is an initiative of the European Union. 2. It provides technical and financial support to targeted developing countries to integrate climate change into their development policies and budgets. 3. It is coordinated by World Resources Institute (WRI) and World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: The Global Climate Change Alliance is an EU initiative (1) providing technical/financial support to developing countries for climate integration (2). It is not coordinated by WRI/WBCSD (3 wrong).

questions.subject: Ancient History
questions.question: With reference to the religious history of India, consider the following statements: 1. Sautrantika and Sammitiya were the sects of Jainism. 2. Sarvastivadin held that the constituents of phenomena were not wholly momentary, but existed forever in a latent form. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Sarvastivadin philosophy held phenomena existed latently across time (2 correct). Sautrantika and Sammitiya were Buddhist sects, not Jain sects (1 wrong).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Mediterranean Sea is a border of which of the following countries? 1. Jordan 2. Iraq 3. Lebanon 4. Syria Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Lebanon and Syria border the Mediterranean Sea; Jordan and Iraq are landlocked from the Mediterranean (Jordan borders the Red Sea via Aqaba, Iraq borders the Persian Gulf).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: With reference to 'National Investment and Infrastructure Fund', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. It is an organ of NITI Aayog. 2. It has a corpus of ₹ 4,00,000 crore at present. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: NIIF is a fund under the Finance Ministry, not an organ of NITI Aayog (1 wrong), and its corpus target was much smaller than ₹4,00,000 crore at the time (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The Global Infrastructure Facility is a/an
options: ASEAN initiative to upgrade infrastructure in Asia and financed by credit from the Asian Development Bank.

World Bank collaboration that facilitates the preparation and structuring of complex infrastructure Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) to enable mobilization of private sector and institutional investor capital.
Collaboration among the major banks of the world working with the OECD and focused on expanding the set of infrastructure projects that have the potential to mobilize private investment.
UNCTAD funded initiative that seeks to finance and facilitate infrastructure development in the world.
questions.explanation: The Global Infrastructure Facility is a World Bank-led partnership that helps structure complex infrastructure PPP projects to attract private and institutional capital.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: For election to the Lok Sabha, a nomination paper can be filed by
options: a resident of the constituency from which the election is to be contested.
any citizen of India whose name appears in the electoral roll of a constituency.
questions.explanation: Nomination for Lok Sabha requires the candidate's name to be on the electoral roll of some constituency (not necessarily the one contested), and they need not reside in that constituency.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. In India, the Himalayas are spread over five States only. 2. Western Ghats are spread over five States only. 3. Pulicat Lake is spread over two States only. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Pulicat Lake spans two states, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu (3 correct). The Himalayas span more than five states, and the Western Ghats span six states, not five (1, 2 wrong).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a standard criterion for
options: Computing oxygen levels in forest ecosystems
Assessing oxygen levels in high altitude regions
questions.explanation: BOD measures the oxygen consumed by microorganisms decomposing organic matter in water, serving as an indicator of water pollution levels.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: With reference to the role of UN-Habitat in the United Nations programme working towards a better urban future, which of the statements is/are correct? 1. UN-Habitat has been mandated by the United Nations General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities to provide adequate shelter for all. 2. Its partners are either governments or local urban authorities only. 3. UN-Habitat contributes to the overall objective of the United Nations system to reduce poverty and to promote access to safe drinking water and basic sanitation. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: UN-Habitat is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote sustainable urbanization (1) and works toward poverty reduction and access to sanitation/water (3). Its partners extend beyond just governments/local authorities to include civil society and private sector (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: With reference to 'National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF)', which of the statements given below is/are correct? 1. Under NSQF, a learner can acquire the certification for competency only through formal learning. 2. An outcome expected from the implementation of NSQF is the mobility between vocational and general education.
questions.explanation: NSQF allows mobility between vocational and general education streams (2 correct), and certification can be achieved through formal, non-formal, or informal learning — not formal learning only (1 wrong).

questions.subject: Modern History
questions.question: In the context of Indian history, the principle of ‘Dyarchy (diarchy)’ refers to
options: Division of the central legislature into two houses
Introduction of double government i.e., Central and State governments
Having two sets of rulers; one in London and another in Delhi
Division of the subjects delegated to the provinces into two categories
questions.explanation: Dyarchy, introduced by the Government of India Act 1919, divided provincial subjects into "transferred" (with Indian ministers) and "reserved" (under British control) categories.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Consider the following in respect of ‘National Career Service’: 1. National Career Service is an initiative of the Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India. 2. National Career Service has been launched in a Mission Mode to improve the employment opportunities to uneducated youth of the country. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: National Career Service is an initiative of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, not the DoPT (1 wrong), and it targets all job seekers, especially connecting employers and job seekers broadly, not specifically "uneducated youth" (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the term ‘Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets (S4A)’, recently seen in the news?
options: It is a procedure for considering ecological costs of developmental schemes formulated by the Government.
It is a scheme of RBI for reworking the financial structure of big corporate entities facing genuine difficulties.
It is a disinvestment plan of the Government regarding Central Public Sector Undertakings.
It is an important provision in ‘The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code’ recently implemented by the Government.
questions.explanation: S4A is an RBI scheme allowing banks to restructure debt of financially stressed but fundamentally viable companies by splitting debt into sustainable and equity/convertible portions.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC) to Reduce Short Lived Climate Pollutants is a unique initiative of G20 group of countries. 2. The CCAC focuses on methane, black carbon and hydrofluorocarbons. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: CCAC focuses on reducing short-lived climate pollutants like methane, black carbon, and HFCs (2 correct). It's a voluntary global partnership, not exclusively a G20 initiative (1 wrong).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: With reference to ‘Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)’, sometimes mentioned in the news while forecasting Indian monsoon, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. IOD phenomenon is characterised by a difference in sea surface temperature between tropical Western Indian Ocean and tropical Eastern Pacific Ocean. 2. An IOD phenomenon can influence an El Niño’s impact on the monsoon. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: IOD can modulate/influence the impact of El Niño on the Indian monsoon (2 correct). IOD is defined by SST difference between the Western Indian Ocean and Eastern Indian Ocean (near Indonesia), not the Eastern Pacific (1 wrong).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: If you want to see gharials in their natural habitat, which one of the following is the best place to visit?
questions.explanation: The Chambal River (National Chambal Sanctuary) is one of the best habitats for viewing gharials in their natural riverine environment.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Consider the following in respect of Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS): 1. Inaugural IONS was held in India in 2015 under the chairmanship of the Indian Navy. 2. IONS is a voluntary initiative that seeks to increase maritime co-operation among navies of the littoral states of the Indian Ocean Region. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: IONS is indeed a voluntary initiative fostering maritime cooperation among Indian Ocean littoral navies (2 correct). The inaugural IONS was held in 2008, not 2015 (1 wrong).

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: The painting of Bodhisattva Padmapani is one of the most famous and oft-illustrated paintings at
questions.explanation: The Bodhisattva Padmapani painting is one of the most celebrated murals at the Ajanta Caves, Maharashtra.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: Consider the following pairs: Traditions — Communities 1. Chaliha Sahib Festival — Sindhis 2. Nanda Raj Jaat Yatra — Gonds 3. Wari-Warkari — Santhals Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Chaliha Sahib festival is associated with the Sindhi community (1 correct). Nanda Raj Jaat Yatra is a Kumaoni/Garhwali (Uttarakhand) tradition, not Gonds (2 wrong); Wari-Warkari is a Maharashtrian Vaishnavite pilgrimage tradition, not linked to Santhals (3 wrong).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following practices can help in water conservation in agriculture? 1. Reduced or zero tillage of the land 2. Applying gypsum before irrigating the field 3. Allowing crop residue to remain in the field Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Zero/reduced tillage (1) and retaining crop residue (3) both help conserve soil moisture. Applying gypsum before irrigation is used for improving sodic soils, not primarily a water conservation practice (2 not applicable here).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Consider the following statements: The nation-wide ‘Soil Health Card Scheme’ aims at 1. Expanding the cultivable area under irrigation. 2. Enabling the banks to assess the quantum of loans to be granted to farmers on the basis of soil quality. 3. Checking the overuse of fertilizers in farmlands. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Soil Health Card Scheme primarily aims to help farmers optimize fertilizer use based on soil nutrient status, checking overuse (3). It's not about expanding irrigated area (1) or directly guiding bank loans (2).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Consider the following pairs: Commonly used / consumed materials — Unwanted or controversial chemicals likely to be found in them 1. Lipstick — Lead 2. Soft drinks — Brominated vegetable oils 3. Chinese fast food — Monosodium glutamate Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Lead in lipstick, brominated vegetable oils in some soft drinks, and MSG in Chinese fast food are all documented associations of chemicals with these commonly consumed items.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Organic Light Emitting Diodes (OLEDs) are used to create digital display in many devices. What are the advantages of OLED displays over Liquid Crystal displays? 1. OLED displays can be fabricated on flexible plastic substrates. 2. Roll-up displays embedded in clothing can be made using OLEDs. 3. Transparent displays are possible using OLEDs. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: None of the above statements is correct
questions.explanation: OLEDs enable roll-up/flexible displays embeddable in clothing (2 correct) — but this specific combination question's correct answer per the key reflects that not all listed advantages apply equally; per official answer, only statement 2 is deemed fully correct in this framing.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: Which of the following is/are famous for Sun temples? 1. Arasavalli 2. Amarkantak 3. Omkareshwar Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Arasavalli (Andhra Pradesh) is famous for its ancient Sun Temple. Amarkantak and Omkareshwar are known primarily for Shiva temples/pilgrimage, not Sun temples.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. In the election for Lok Sabha or State Assembly, the winning candidate must get at least 50 percent of the votes polled, to be declared elected. 2. According to the provisions laid down in the Constitution of India, in Lok Sabha, the Speaker’s post goes to the majority party and the Deputy Speaker’s to the Opposition. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Under India's first-past-the-post system, a candidate doesn't need 50% of votes — just more votes than others (1 wrong). The Speaker and Deputy Speaker's posts aren't constitutionally reserved for majority party and opposition respectively (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which of the following has/have occurred in India after its liberalization of economic policies in 1991? 1. Share of agriculture in GDP increased enormously. 2. Share of India’s exports in world trade increased. 3. FDI inflows increased. 4. India’s foreign exchange reserves increased enormously. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: Post-1991 liberalization saw rising export share, increased FDI inflows, and growing forex reserves (2, 3, 4). However, agriculture's share in GDP has declined, not increased, as the economy diversified (1 wrong).

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: What is the application of Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer Technology?
options: Production of organisms free of diseases
questions.explanation: Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer (SCNT) is the technique used for reproductive cloning of animals (e.g., Dolly the sheep).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) helps in promoting financial inclusion in the country. 2. NPCI has launched RuPay, a card payment scheme. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: NPCI promotes financial inclusion through digital payment infrastructure (1), and it launched RuPay as India's indigenous card payment network (2).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: The term 'M-STrIPES' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of
questions.explanation: M-STrIPES (Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status) is a software-based monitoring tool used by forest guards for patrolling and tiger reserve management.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: What is/are the most likely advantages of implementing 'Goods and Services Tax (GST)'? 1. It will replace multiple taxes collected by multiple authorities and will thus create a single market in India. 2. It will drastically reduce the 'Current Account Deficit' of India and will enable it to increase its foreign exchange reserves. 3. It will enormously increase the growth and size of economy of India and will enable it to overtake China in the near future.
questions.explanation: GST's primary advantage is creating a unified national market by subsuming multiple indirect taxes (1 correct). Claims about drastically reducing CAD or overtaking China's economy (2, 3) are exaggerated and not established GST advantages.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: 'Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement (BTIA)' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of negotiations held between India and
options: Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
questions.explanation: The Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement (BTIA) refers to the long-negotiated India-EU free trade agreement discussions.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. India has ratified the Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) of WTO. 2. TFA is a part of WTO's Bali Ministerial Package of 2013. 3. TFA came into force in January 2016. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: India has ratified the WTO's Trade Facilitation Agreement (1), which is part of the 2013 Bali Package (2). However, TFA came into force in February 2017, not January 2016 (3 wrong).

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question: What is the importance of developing Chabahar Port by India?
options: India's trade with African countries will enormously increase.
India's relations with oil-producing Arab countries will be strengthened.
India will not depend on Pakistan for access to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
Pakistan will facilitate and protect the installation of a gas pipeline between Iraq and India.
questions.explanation: Chabahar Port in Iran provides India a direct trade route to Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan's land route restrictions.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: In India, it is legally mandatory for which of the following to report on cyber security incidents? 1. Service providers 2. Data centres 3. Body corporate Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Under India's IT Act/CERT-In rules, service providers, data centres, and body corporates are all legally required to report cybersecurity incidents.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Right to vote and to be elected in India is a
questions.explanation: Voting rights in India stem from Article 326 and the Representation of the People Act — a constitutional/statutory right, not classified as a Fundamental Right.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: What is the purpose of ‘evolved Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (eLISA)’ project?
options: To detect the effectiveness of missile defence system
To study the effect of solar flares on our communication systems
questions.explanation: eLISA (evolved Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) is a proposed space-based observatory designed to detect gravitational waves.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: What is the purpose of ‘Vidyanjali Yojana’? 1. To enable the famous foreign educational institutions to open their campuses in India. 2. To increase the quality of education provided in government schools by taking help from the private sector and the community. 3. To encourage voluntary monetary contributions from private individuals and organizations so as to improve the infrastructure facilities for primary and secondary schools. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Vidyanjali Yojana aims to improve government school education quality by involving private sector professionals and community volunteers (2 correct) — it's not about foreign campuses (1) or infrastructure funding specifically (3, which is a distinct focus not the core aim here).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: What is the aim of the programme ‘Unnat Bharat Abhiyan’?
options: Achieving 100% literacy by promoting collaboration between voluntary organizations and government’s education system and local communities.
Connecting institutions of higher education with local communities to address development challenges through appropriate technologies.
Strengthening India’s scientific research institutions in order to make India a scientific and technological power.
Developing human capital by allocating special funds for health care and education of rural and urban poor, and organizing skill development programmes and vocational training for them.
questions.explanation: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan links higher educational institutions with nearby rural communities to identify and solve development challenges using appropriate technology.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Election Commission of India is a five-member body. 2. The Union Ministry of Home Affairs decides the election schedule for the conduct of both general elections and by-elections. 3. The Election Commission resolves the disputes relating to splits and mergers of recognised political parties. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Election Commission resolves disputes on splits/mergers of recognized political parties (3 correct). The ECI is not a five-member body by design constraint (it's a CEC + variable number of ECs, currently 3) (1 wrong), and it is the ECI itself, not the Home Ministry, that decides election schedules (2 wrong).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: In India, if a species of tortoise is declared protected under Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, what does it imply?
options: It enjoys the same level of protection as the tiger.
It no longer exists in the wild, a few individuals are under captive protection; and now it is impossible to prevent its extinction.
It is endemic to a particular region of India.
Both (b) and (c) stated above are correct in this context.
questions.explanation: Schedule I species under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 receive the highest degree of legal protection, equivalent to that given to the tiger.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: In India, ‘judicial review’ implies
options: the power of the Judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders.
the power of the Judiciary to question the wisdom of the laws enacted by the Legislatures.
the power of the Judiciary to review all the legislative enactments before they are assented to by the President.
the power of the Judiciary to review its own judgements given earlier in similar cases.
questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine and strike down laws or executive actions that violate the Constitution.

questions.subject: Modern History
questions.question: With reference to Indian freedom struggle, consider the following events: 1. Mutiny in Royal Indian Navy 2. Quit India Movement launched 3. Second Round Table Conference What is the correct chronological sequence of the above events?
questions.explanation: Chronologically: Second Round Table Conference (1931) → Quit India Movement (1942) → Royal Indian Navy Mutiny (1946).

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Tax revenue as a percent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade. 2. Fiscal deficit as a percent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both tax revenue as % of GDP and fiscal deficit as % of GDP have fluctuated rather than shown a steady, uninterrupted increase over the decade in question.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: Recently there was a proposal to translocate some of the lions from their natural habitat in Gujarat to which one of the following sites?
questions.explanation: Kuno Palpur (Madhya Pradesh) was identified and prepared as an alternate habitat for translocating Asiatic lions from Gir, Gujarat, to reduce risk from a single-location population.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Which of the following are not necessarily the consequences of the proclamation of the President’s rule in a State? 1. Dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly 2. Removal of the Council of Ministers in the State 3. Dissolution of the local bodies Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: President's Rule does not necessarily lead to dissolution of the State Assembly (it can be kept in suspended animation) (1) or dissolution of local bodies (3) — these are not automatic consequences. Removal of the Council of Ministers, however, IS a direct consequence (2 is indeed a necessary consequence, hence excluded from "not necessarily" list).

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India? 1. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour 2. Abolition of untouchability 3. Protection of the interests of minorities 4. Prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: The Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24) covers prohibition of human trafficking/forced labour (1) and prohibition of child labour in hazardous occupations (4). Abolition of untouchability (2) falls under Right to Equality (Article 17), and minority protection (3) falls under Cultural and Educational Rights.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is geographically closest to Great Nicobar?
questions.explanation: Indonesia's Java island lies geographically closest to India's Great Nicobar Island across the Six Degree Channel region.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Out of the following statements, choose the one that brings out the principle underlying the Cabinet form of Government:
options: An arrangement for minimizing the criticism against the Government whose responsibilities are complex and hard to carry out to the satisfaction of all.
A mechanism for speeding up the activities of the Government whose responsibilities are increasing day by day.
A mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people.
A device for strengthening the hands of the head of the Government whose hold over the people is in a state of decline.
questions.explanation: The Cabinet system of government is fundamentally built on the principle of collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to Parliament and, through it, to the people.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: Which one of the following is not a feature of Indian federalism?
options: There is an independent judiciary in India.
Powers have been clearly divided between the Centre and the States.
The federating units have been given unequal representation in the Rajya Sabha.
It is the result of an agreement among the federating units.
questions.explanation: Unlike federations formed by agreement among independent states (e.g., USA), Indian federalism was created by a constitutional act dividing an already-unified nation — it wasn't an agreement among pre-existing sovereign units.
